verdict.rationale: YYLO can ingest a reported bug (e.g., a GitHub issue) into its kanban ledger, spin up a coding-agent subagent to work an isolated task worktree, and iterate ('run-until-completion') until kanban work is done, which supports an agent-driven fix loop. However, docs explicitly state tests/semantic review are 'explicit project checks outside merge' and merge 'launches no models, chooses no reviewers' — so the diagnose-and-verify-fix loop is not autonomous end-to-end; a human or separate check step is required. Missing for 10: evidence of the agent performing bug diagnosis/root-cause reasoning, automated verification that the fix resolves the reported issue, and an end-to-end autonomous close-the-loop example.
